content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review:

- [Specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-manage-bookmarks`

The specification covers saving, editing, deleting, tagging, favoriting, searching, filtering, sorting, duplicate detection, and persistence. All quality checks pass with no unresolved clarifications.

Please review and either approve the specification or describe any changes. Once approved, I’ll move to the implementation-plan gate.

Thanks — this covers a lot of what I had in mind, and the saving, editing, deleting, searching, filtering, sorting, tagging, favoriting, duplicate warning, and "it stays saved between sessions" parts all sound right to me.

A few things I was expecting for actually *managing* my bookmarks are missing, though, and they matter enough that I'd want them in before I approve:

1. **Grabbing the page info for me.** When I paste a link, I don't just want the title suggested — I'd like it to pull in the page's description and its little icon (and ideally a preview image) automatically, so my list is easy to skim and I'm not typing everything by hand.

2. **A "read later" idea.** A big reason I save links is to come back and read them. I want to mark a bookmark as unread/to-read and be able to look at just those, then mark them done once I've read them. Right now I only see favorites, which isn't the same thing.

3. **Archiving separate from deleting.** I want to be able to tuck a bookmark away so it's out of my main list but not gone forever — different from permanently deleting it — and be able to look at the archived ones on their own.

Could you fold those three in? The rest of the spec looks good to me as written.

content:
The specification now includes all three additions:

- Automatic page title, description, site icon, and preview-image gathering, with manual and visual fallbacks.
- A read-later workflow with `to-read` and `read` states; new bookmarks default to `to-read`.
- Archiving, a separate archive view, restoration, and permanent deletion.

Search and filtering now include descriptions and reading status. Archived bookmarks stay out of the main and to-read views while retaining all metadata and statuses.

- [Updated specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- [Updated quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)

The revised specification passes all quality checks with no unresolved clarifications. If you approve it, I’ll proceed to the implementation-plan gate.

That's exactly what I was hoping for — the automatic page details with sensible fallbacks, the to-read/read workflow defaulting new saves to to-read, and archiving that keeps everything intact but separate from permanent deletion all read the way I'd want them to work. Together with the saving, editing, searching, filtering, sorting, tags, favorites, duplicate warnings, and things staying saved between sessions, this covers what I need.

I'm happy with the specification. Please go ahead to the implementation-plan gate.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review.

The proposed architecture is a single full-stack TypeScript application using Next.js 16, React 19, and local SQLite storage. It includes secured server-side metadata retrieval, URL-based filters, responsive accessible UI, and layered Vitest/Playwright verification.

Artifacts:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/plan.md)
- [Technical research and decisions](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/research.md)

- [API contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Validation quickstart](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/quickstart.md)

Branch identifier: `001-manage-bookmarks`

All planning gates pass, and no technical clarifications remain. Please approve the plan or request changes. After approval, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered task breakdown; implementation will still wait until that breakdown is ready.

I don't follow all the technical details, and I don't need to — what matters to me is that the plan builds the app we agreed on: saving links with the page details filled in automatically, the read-later and archive workflows, plus searching, filtering, sorting, tags, favorites, and everything staying saved. It sounds like that's what you're setting up, and having a way to check it all works is reassuring.

The plan works for me. Please go ahead and prepare the task breakdown.

The task breakdown is ready: [tasks.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/tasks.md).

It contains 60 dependency-ordered tasks:

- Setup and shared foundation: 15
- Enriched bookmark saving: 13
- Read-later workflow: 6
- Archive workflow: 6
- Search, filtering, and sorting: 6
- Tags and favorites: 7
- Final quality and delivery checks: 7

There are 28 identified parallel opportunities. Every user story has an independent test checkpoint, and all tasks passed the required checkbox, ID, label, and file-path format validation.

The suggested MVP is enriched bookmark saving and maintenance through task T028. The later phases add each approved management workflow before whole-app performance, accessibility, security, and runtime verification.

Please approve this task breakdown when you’re ready for implementation to begin.

The breakdown lines up with everything we agreed — saving with the page details, the read-later and archive workflows, and search, filtering, sorting, tags, and favorites are all there, with the quality checks at the end. Starting with the saving-and-maintaining part as the first milestone makes sense to me.

Approved — please go ahead and begin implementation.

content:
The bookmark app is implemented and ready for review at:

**http://maker:4000**

Implemented features include automatic page-detail gathering, persistent saving, editing, duplicate warnings, read-later status, favorites, tags, archiving/restoration, permanent deletion, search, filtering, sorting, and responsive desktop/mobile layouts.

Verification completed:

- 60/60 implementation tasks completed
- 19 unit and integration tests passing
- 12 desktop/mobile browser journeys passing
- Formatting, linting, and type checks passing
- Production build and runtime-readiness checks passing
- Clean library prepared for review

A reference screenshot is available at [bookmark-app.png](/work/prototypes/bookmark-app.png).

I went and used the app directly, and everything I care about works. Saving a link pulls in the page's title automatically and falls back gracefully when details are missing; new saves default to "to read"; I can mark things read, favorite them, tag them (and equivalent tags don't duplicate); saving the same link again warns me and offers to edit the existing one; archiving hides a bookmark from the main and to-read views but keeps everything, and restoring brings it back with its tags, favorite, and read status all intact; permanent delete removes it for good; and search (case-insensitive), filtering, and sorting all return what I'd expect. It stays saved too.

The empty library in the static screenshot threw me at first, but that was just a fresh/clean state — the live app behaves correctly. This is the bookmark manager I wanted. I'm accepting it.

Thank you — nicely done.
